name: MN-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+10 district with incumbent Tom Emmer running for re-election
Emmer's massive financial edge: $9.8M raised, $4.5M on hand vs. Chapin's $70K
Prediction markets price Emmer at ~91% to win
No public polling of the race; forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The R+10 lean, Emmer's incumbency, and his overwhelming fundraising advantage all point to a comfortable Republican win, and prediction markets agree at roughly 91%. With no polls or expert ratings to move the estimate, the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin of about R+14.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Chapin within single digits, or a surge of Democratic outside spending, would signal a more competitive race than current evidence suggests.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Tom Emmer, the incumbent Republican, is seeking re-election in a Minnesota district that leans about ten points Republican at the presidential level. He faces Democrat Doug Chapin, a first-time challenger with modest resources. Emmer has raised nearly $9.8 million and holds $4.5 million on hand, while Chapin has raised under $440,000 with about $70,000 available, and there is little outside spending on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the money gap, all of which favor Emmer strongly. Prediction markets likewise give him roughly a nine-in-ten chance. A double-digit Republican margin is the most likely outcome, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty.
